title: Downregulated RSAD2 Attenuates the Apoptosis of LPS-Stimulated RAW264.7 via NF-κB Signaling Pathway
authors: Zhen Qi; Kongli Lu; Mengxi Huang; Haixia Wang; Rongheng Liao; Ri Tang
id: Matched: RSAD2 Knockdown Attenuated Apoptosis in LPS-Induced RAW264.7 Cells
abstract: This study investigated RSAD2's role in LPS-stimulated macrophage apoptosis. Downregulating RSAD2 reduces apoptosis by suppressing the NF-κB pathway.

title: Epigenetic profile in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages
authors: Ester Correia Sarmento Rios; Thais Martins Lima Salgado; Francisco Garcia Soriano

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni, Yanal Ghosheh, Akula Bala Pramod, Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

title: RSAD2: A pathogenic interferon-stimulated gene at the maternal-fetal interface of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus
authors: Xiaoyu Ding; Yonggang Zhou; Xiaofeng Qiu; Xiuxiu Xu; Xinyu Hu; Jingkun Qin; Yulan Chen; Min Zhang; J...
abstract: This study identifies RSAD2 as a pathogenic interferon-stimulated gene at the maternal-fetal interface in systemic lupus erythematosus patients. Elevated RSAD2 impairs placental vascular development by accumulating diacylglycerol lipids, suggesting RSAD2 targeting as a therapeutic strategy.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced innate immune responses are exacerbated by Prohibitin 1 deficiency and mitigated by S-adenosylmethionine in murine macrophages
authors: Soohan Jung; Jaehee Park; Kwang Suk Ko
id: Matched: Effect of LPS stimulation on Phb1 expression in RAW 264.7 cells
abstract: Prohibitin 1 deficiency exacerbates LPS-induced inflammation in macrophages, while S-adenosylmethionine mitigates these responses. Phb1 modulates innate immunity via the NF-κB pathway.

title: LncRNA NRIR inhibits osteogenesis by promoting macrophage M1 polarization through RSAD2/NF-κB axis in peri-implantitis
authors: Renshengjie Zhao; Lan Wang; Yang Zhou; Keming Xiao; Qiqi Liu; Ke Yu
id: Matched: RSAD2 regulates M1 macrophage polarization
abstract: LncRNA NRIR's role in peri-implantitis macrophage polarization was studied. NRIR promotes M1 macrophage polarization via the RSAD2/NF-κB axis, inhibiting osteogenesis.

title: Full Spectrum of LPS Activation in Alveolar Macrophages of Healthy Volunteers by Whole Transcriptomic Profiling
authors: Miguel Pinilla-Vera, Zeyu Xiong, Yutong Zhao, Jing Zhao, Michael P. Donahoe, Suchitra Barge, William...
abstract: Human alveolar macrophages were studied for their response to LPS activation using transcriptomic profiling. LPS induced a type I interferon signature, with IRF-7 and USP18 potentially fine-tuning IL-10 production.

title: Lipopolysaccharide from biofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 induces macrophage hyperinflammatory responses
authors: Sufei Wang; Dandan Xiang; Fangbing Tian; Ming Ni
abstract: Biofilm-forming *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* LPS was studied for its effect on macrophage polarization. This LPS induced hyperinflammatory responses and increased bacterial growth in macrophages compared to planktonic LPS.

title: Histone deacetylase 2 is essential for LPS‐induced inflammatory responses in macrophages
authors: Chenming Wu; Ang Li; Jian Hu; Jiuhong Kang
id: Matched: BMM adoptive transfer, LPS challenge and bacterial sepsis model
abstract: Histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) is essential for LPS-induced inflammatory responses in macrophages. HDAC2 regulates these responses by deacetylating c-Jun, which then represses pro-inflammatory gene transcription.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-Activated Macrophages Suppress Cellular Senescence and Promote Rejuvenation in Human Dermal Fibroblasts
authors: Hiroyuki Inagawa; Chie Kohchi; Miyuki Uehiro; Gen-Ichiro Soma
abstract: LPS-activated macrophages were studied for their effect on senescent human dermal fibroblasts. Their secretions suppressed senescence and partially rejuvenated aged fibroblasts.

title: RSAD2 is abundant in atherosclerotic plaques and promotes interferon-induced CXCR3-chemokines in human smooth muscle cells
authors: Assim Hayderi; Ashok K. Kumawat; Vladimir S. Shavva; Mats Dreifaldt; Birgitta Sigvant; Marcelo H. Pe...
id: Matched: IFN-γ strongly and persistently induces RSAD2 in hAoSMCs
abstract: RSAD2 was studied in atherosclerotic plaques and IFN-γ-stimulated human smooth muscle cells. RSAD2 promotes interferon-induced CXCR3-chemokines in these cells, potentially contributing to monocyte recruitment in atherosclerosis.

title: Species-Specificity of Transcriptional Regulation and the Response to Lipopolysaccharide in Mammalian Macrophages
authors: Stephen J. Bush; Mary E. B. McCulloch; Zofia M. Lisowski; Charity Muriuki; Emily L. Clark; Rachel Yo...
abstract: This study analyzed the transcriptional response of sheep macrophages to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and compared it to other mammalian species. A conserved transcriptional network was found, but large animals and rodents differed in their metabolic responses to LPS.

title: Rsad2 is necessary for mouse dendritic cell maturation via the IRF7-mediated signaling pathway
authors: Ji-Su Jang; Jun-Ho Lee; Nam-Chul Jung; So-Yeon Choi; Soo-Yeoun Park; Ji-Young Yoo; Jie-Young Song; H...
id: Matched: Expression of Rsad2 in mDCs
abstract: Rsad2 expression was studied in mouse dendritic cells and its role in maturation investigated. Rsad2 is essential for dendritic cell maturation through the IRF7 pathway and is required for their anti-tumor efficacy.

title: Intracellular NAD+ levels are associated with LPS-induced TNF-α release in pro-inflammatory macrophages
authors: Abbas Jawad Al-Shabany; Alan John Moody; Andrew David Foey; Richard Andrew Billington
abstract: Intracellular NAD+ levels were studied in pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. NAD+ levels in pro-inflammatory macrophages correlated with TNF-α release.

title: Selection of reliable reference genes for the normalisation of gene expression levels following time course LPS stimulation of murine bone marrow derived macrophages
authors: Akane Tanaka, Joyce To, Bronwyn O’Brien, Sheila Donnelly, Maria Lund
abstract: This study assessed the stability of eight common reference genes in LPS-stimulated murine macrophages. It found that some traditional genes are unreliable, and identified two new, stable reference genes for accurate gene expression analysis.

title: Oral and transdermal administration of lipopolysaccharide safely enhances self-healing ability through the macrophage network
authors: Gen-Ichiro Soma; Masataka Oda; Vindy Tjendana Tjhin; Chie Kohchi; Hiroyuki Inagawa
id: Matched: Regulation of innate immunity by LPS as an environmental agent
abstract: Oral and transdermal LPS administration was studied for its effects on self-healing. This method safely enhances healing through a "macrophage network" involving mucosal immune cells.

title: Expression Profiling of LPS Responsive miRNA in Primary Human Macrophages
authors: Afsar Raza Naqvi, Sheng Zhong, Hong Dang, Jezrom B Fordham, Salvador Nares, Asma Khan
abstract: This study profiled microRNA expression in human macrophages exposed to lipopolysaccharide (LPS). LPS treatment temporally altered macrophage microRNA expression, impacting key cell signaling and pathogen response pathways.

title: A potential role for macrophages in maintaining lipopolysaccharide-induced subacute airway inflammation in rats
authors: LIN LIU; LEI CHEN; YONGSHENG WANG; HUA YANG; YIFANG CHEN; XIAOYA XU; HANG ZHOU; FANGPING JIANG; TONG...
abstract: This study investigated airway inflammation in rats after lipopolysaccharide administration. Macrophages, along with IL-1β, showed sustained presence, suggesting their role in maintaining this inflammation.

title: P23 Acts as Functional RBP in the Macrophage Inflammation Response
authors: Sebastian de Vries; Vladimir Benes; Isabel S. Naarmann-de Vries; Cornelia Rücklé; Katharina Zarnack;...
id: Matched: Depletion of P23 Enhances Phagocytosis
abstract: P23, a known HSP90 co-chaperone, was studied for its RNA-binding role in macrophages. P23 depletion destabilizes Kif15 mRNA, reducing KIF15 expression and enhancing macrophage migration and phagocytosis.

abstract: A new LC-MS/MS assay simultaneously measures arginine and sulfur amino acid metabolism. This assay revealed that the Cit+Orn/Arg+Asp ratio is an early, sensitive biomarker of LPS-induced macrophage activation.

title: Mathematical modelling of activation-induced heterogeneity reveals cell state transitions underpinning macrophage responses to LPS
authors: S. Dey, D. Boucher, J. W. Pitchford, D. Lagos *
id: Matched: Macrophage community AIH is dependent on LPS dose
abstract: This study mathematically models macrophage responses to LPS, analyzing single-cell protein expression. Macrophage hypo-responsiveness to secondary LPS challenges is driven by altered transition rates to non-responsive states.

title: Role and mechanism of miR-144-5p in LPS-induced macrophages
authors: Guozhu Zhou; Yuwei Li; Jianping Ni; Ping Jiang; Zili Bao
abstract: This study investigated miR-144-5p's role in LPS-induced macrophages. miR-144-5p overexpression reduced cell viability and inflammatory cytokine expression by targeting TLR2 and inhibiting NF-κB signaling.
